title: Killing the Case for Randomization in Dynamic Assortment Optimization
summary: One of the traditional approaches for constructing approximate policies for dynamic assortment optimization problems is to use sampling-based inventory-agnostic policies. Such policies are called sampling-based, as they sample an assortment of products from a fixed distribution at each time period to offer to a customer of each type. Such policies are called inventory-agnostic, as the sampled assortments may include products without remaining inventories, so if a customer chooses a product without remaining inventories, then she leaves without a purchase.
